title: Fibonacci EA v5.0 M30 Timeframe Transition Test
research_question: Does transitioning execution from M15 to M30 filter out entry candlestick wick noise, improve trade win-rate and payoff, and generate higher net profit than baseline EXP-0008 ($577.65) while keeping max equity drawdown <= 8.0% on GBPUSD across the 5-year training partition?
hypothesis: Executing entry signals on M30 candles while scanning market structure on H1 reduces false breakout wicks, resulting in higher win rate, lower drawdown, and greater net profitability than baseline EXP-0008.

facts: EXP-0008 executed on M15 achieved $577.65 profit and 7.35% drawdown, but suffered from 1:2.76 payoff asymmetry due to M15 wick noise.
The EA detects swing structure on H1 bars (25-500 pips), making M30 candles a closer structural match for pullback confirmation than M15.
inferences: M30 candlestick patterns (hammer, engulfing, pin bars) have higher predictive reliability than M15 patterns.
Filtering lower-timeframe noise will reduce false entries and prevent premature stop-outs.
evidence: EXP-0008 total_trades=272, profit_factor=1.39, win_rate=79.38%, total_net_profit=577.65, equity_drawdown_maximal_percent=7.35

independent_variables.name: timeframe
independent_variables.rationale: Transition execution chart timeframe from M15 to M30 to filter lower-timeframe wick noise and improve candle confirmation reliability.

assumptions: Broker tick history supports accurate M30 bar construction across 2020-2024.
expected_observations: Total net profit will be positive and comparable to or exceeding baseline $577.65.
falsification_conditions: Maximum equity drawdown exceeds 8.0%, breaching the prop firm guard threshold.
